description: #5057 — `undo_page_group`, the grouped positional undo. Like `undo_page_op` its `depth` is an ordinal and `windowMs` is the fixture's own literal, so the group is deterministic where an `OpRef`-addressed undo would not be. The group deliberately holds ops of two DIFFERENT types: the return is a LIST of `UndoResult`, one headed row per element, and two identical rows would pin the count while leaving the order free. Reversed newest-first, the rows read `set_property` then `create_block`, so a group that reversed the right ops in the wrong sequence fails here even though the settled snapshot would be identical.

blocks.content: keeps its row, loses its property

name: undo_page_group

ops.comment: The older op in the group. Undoing a create is always reversible, unlike an edit, which needs a prior text row in the op log.
The newer op, and a different type from the one above so the two returned rows are distinguishable.

A window wide enough to swallow both ops, which run back to back in the harness. The property clears and the created block becomes a tombstone — so the settled state differs from the seed in a way a no-op could not produce.
ops.name: undo_both_ops_as_one_group

ops.comment: `depth must be non-negative` — checked before the lookup, so this is Validation rather than the NotFound an overrun gives.
ops.name: a_negative_depth_is_refused

ops.comment: The second arg carries its own sign guard, so a negative window is refused rather than silently sizing an empty group.
ops.name: a_negative_window_is_refused

queries.comment: The observation: the created block is gone and S2 is still here — the group reversed both of its ops.
queries.name: blocks_after_the_group_undo
